source: a 3d dti but it's called fashion week and you wake up on a bed walk into your closet and pick an outfit a y2k, cute core, or emo or big puffy dresses and you have a 5 minute time limit and when the time is up you go on the runway and people around the world will vote you stars

answers.ask: No theme was stated - should the bedroom and runway read as glossy modern fashion-show, or bright stylized toon?
answers.answer: Use a bright stylized toon look that fits the cute Fashion Week dress-up vibe.

answers.ask: Is the bedroom and closet one shared dressing area everyone uses, or a private copy per player?
answers.answer: Give each player a private bedroom and closet so everyone can pick their outfit without crowding.

scene_prompt: Create a bright stylized-toon 3D fashion dress-up map with private bedroom-and-closet dressing suites for each player. Each suite begins at a bed and opens into a personal closet area displaying outfit options including Y2K, cute-core, emo, and large puffy dresses. Connect the dressing area to a glossy fashion-show runway, with a clear catwalk and viewing space arranged around it for spectators.
blob:
### Genre
The dominant genre is Roleplay & Avatar Sim, specifically a dress-up experience: players prepare an avatar look and present it on a runway. No secondary genre is needed.

### Shape and preset
Use `stage-runway`, matching the Dress Up preset. This is a fashion-show venue rather than a town: private preparation suites feed a central catwalk, and all viewing orientation faces the runway. The prompt keeps the preset’s defining stage-and-dressing-room arrangement, while making the dressing spaces private rather than communal.

### Config requirements
No additional image-config option is required. The private bedroom-and-closet suites, outfit displays, catwalk, and surrounding audience space are intrinsic scene geometry of `stage-runway`; do not add unrequested photo vignettes, town circulation, or ambient NPCs.

### Layout requirements
Nothing further needs to be placed against segmentation. Each player’s private-suite assignment, bed arrival point, wardrobe interaction, timing, voting, and show progression are mechanics rather than layout markers.

### Layout components
Build one enclosed fashion-show venue. Place a row or ring of identical private bedroom-and-closet dressing suites behind and to the sides of the show area; the number of suites scales to player capacity, since no count was stated. Each suite starts at a bed and opens into a personal closet/display wall with clearly separated Y2K, cute-core, emo, and large puffy-dress outfit displays. Short private corridors or backstage exits converge on a glossy central runway. The runway is a long, straight catwalk with a presentation end, broad viewing floor along both sides, and sightlines facing inward toward the model path. Keep public viewing circulation separate from suite entrances. Enclose the entire build as one bright interior venue, with polished floors, oversized rounded décor, and no exterior terrain.

### Render order
Use `isometric`: the fashion-show atmosphere, central catwalk, and readable relationship of suites to audience space are the authority; no topology-sensitive route needs a plan-first render.

### Scale, theme, and pipeline cost
Use a medium scale, driven by repeated private suites plus one shared runway and spectator floor. Theme: bright stylized toon, cute Fashion Week glamour, glossy pastel surfaces and playful high-fashion décor. Use `P0`; this is a single-level enclosed venue with no overhangs, separate maps, exterior-to-interior transition, or topology that must be procedurally validated.
